### Decision ledger

**(a) Who controls the source?**
The reported source (`WINDOW_MESSAGE_EVENT` at `js/background.js:342`) is misattributed. Line 342 is inside `outputDevicesToList()` building an HTML `<table>` of device names — it is not a message listener, and a Manifest V3 service worker has no `window`/`postMessage` surface at all. However, reading the real source reveals the actual web-accessible input the DoubleX rule was pointing at: `chrome.runtime.onConnectExternal` at `js/background.js:304`.

`externally_connectable.matches: ["*://*.mazii.net/*"]` means any page whose origin is `https://*.mazii.net` can call `chrome.runtime.connect(extensionId)` and get a port. The listener has **no `sender.id` allowlist and no `sender.origin`/URL check** — it directly attaches `port.onMessage`. (It is also reachable by any other installed extension, since cross-extension connect is not restricted by `externally_connectable`.)

**(b) Source-to-sink path**
```
external page on *.mazii.net
  → chrome.runtime.connect(extId)                       // externally_connectable surface
  → chrome.runtime.onConnectExternal          (bg L304)

sourceReachability.browserFacts: Determine whether web/external code can actually reach this source; do not infer it only from a variable name.

sinkClassification.rule: Confirm that attacker data reaches the actual URL/config/body/code/storage argument and is not replaced by a literal or browser-derived value.

browserTrustRules: sender.id is browser-populated and only a fixed-ID allowlist is an unforgeable inter-extension trust boundary.
event.origin/window.location.origin and message action/type fields are attacker-satisfiable in a page-to-content-script bridge.

chrome.action/browserAction badge, title, icon, and chrome.notifications UI state are extension/browser authority; attacker-controlled operative fields are TP, not harmless presentation. Verify the value reaches the API argument.
A source/sink match in an import statement, comment, dead code, or an unrelated action branch is not a data-flow proof.
For chrome.tabs.create/windows.create/downloads/fetch/WebSocket, verify that the tainted value controls the URL/body/options actually consumed by the API.
